Associations [Only including dataset "Source"]
■ Squares are categorical associations (uncertainty coefficient & correlation ratio) from 0 to 1. The uncertainty coefficient is assymmetrical, (i.e. ROW LABEL values indicate how much they PROVIDE INFORMATION to each LABEL at the TOP).

• Circles are the symmetrical numerical correlations (Pearson's) from -1 to 1. The trivial diagonal is intentionally left blank for clarity.
■ Squares show categorical-categorical associations using the uncertainty coefficient (Theil's U), ranging from 0 to 1.
This measure is assymmetrical: ROW LABEL values indicate how much information the row feature PROVIDES about the column (TOP) feature.
• Circles show the Pearson correlation coefficient between numerical features, ranging from -1 (perfect negative) to 1 (perfect positive).
This measure is symmetrical. The trivial diagonal (self-correlation = 1) is intentionally left blank for clarity.
■ Squares show categorical-numerical associations using the correlation ratio, ranging from 0 (no relationship) to 1 (perfect relationship).
Rows are categorical features, Columns are numerical features.

■ Squares show categorical-categorical associations using the uncertainty coefficient (Theil's U), ranging from 0 to 1.
This measure is assymmetrical: ROW LABEL values indicate how much information the row feature PROVIDES about the column (TOP) feature.
• Circles show the Pearson correlation coefficient between numerical features, ranging from -1 (perfect negative) to 1 (perfect positive).
This measure is symmetrical. The trivial diagonal (self-correlation = 1) is intentionally left blank for clarity.
